notes: Hongshan culture of the West Liao basin; infobox 'c. 4700 to 2900 BC'. Extent: 'the West Liao river basin in northeast China', 'an area stretching from Inner Mongolia to Liaoning'; Hongshanhou 'in Hongshan District, Chifeng'; Niuheliang 'a unique ritual complex'. No area, no site count and no phases with dates ('Early Hongshan' and 'Late Hongshan' are mentioned only for diet). Chifeng 150 km + Chaoyang 120 km are drawn (confidence 2). Predecessors: infobox 'Xinglongwa culture, Xinle culture, Zhaobaogou culture' (Xinglongwa '6200-5400 BC', Xinle '5300-4800 BC' as listed on the page); the Zhaobaogou dossier hands over its Chifeng part in 4700 (page silent). The Xinle (Shenyang) has no dossier. The Yangshao 'existed contemporaneously with the Hongshan culture' and 'interacted'; no border. Successors: infobox 'Xiaoheyan (3000-2000 BCE), Lower Xiajiadian (2200-1600 BCE), and Upper Xiajiadian (1000-600 BCE)'; the Xiaoheyan is the direct successor here (Xiaoheyan starts 3000, 100 years before the Hongshan's end) and has no dossier; the gap 2899..2200 before the Lower Xiajiadian is not drawn by anyone. No area figure.
